pages.title: Revision River Ferry Display Revision
pages.notebookSkill: Revise an observed display detail into a clearer story ending.
pages.visitFit: Adult-led upper-age notebook page for a quiet museum, gallery, or field-trip table after looking at one display.
pages.adultSetup: Invite each writer to choose one exhibit clue, one color, and one shape from a display, then return to the table before writing.
pages.kidDirection: Turn one museum observation into a draft ending, revise it once, and make the final line echo an earlier clue.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which exhibit clue should matter at the ending and which extra detail can drift away from the ferry route.

pageSections.heading: Observation Dock
lines: The exhibit clue I noticed first was ____________________.
The color or shape that could return later is ____________________.
A quiet display detail I might leave out is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Revision Ferry
lines: My first ending idea is ____________________.
One detail I can move closer to the ending is ____________________.
The ending becomes clearer when ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Final Dock
lines: My revised final sentence begins with ____________________.
The observation that echoes the start is ____________________.
The story feeling at the final dock is ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share the exhibit clue that returned in your ending: ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: The revision choice that made my page clearer was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Skip sharing and copy only the revised final line here: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Notice one display pattern elsewhere and add it to this ending: ____________________.

pages.title: Clue Label Tower Focused Label
pages.notebookSkill: Select one useful observation and shape it into a concise exhibit label.
pages.visitFit: Adult-led notebook page for older writers after a short look at one object, case, wall display, or room corner.
pages.adultSetup: Point out that real labels stay brief, then ask writers to invent a new label from one observed clue without copying museum text.
pages.kidDirection: Choose one object clue, decide what readers should notice first, and write a short invented label for a story museum.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which clue earns the first sentence, which detail is only decoration, and how the label can stay clear.

pageSections.heading: Clue Sort

pageSections.heading: Label Choice
lines: Visitors in my story should notice first that ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tower Label

pages.shareLine: Share one focused label word or point to it on your page: ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: The observation I chose instead of many details was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Work quietly by writing only the final exhibit label here: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: At home, write a new label for an ordinary object using one clue: ____________________.

pages.title: Compass Craft Gallery Route
pages.notebookSkill: Use map language to turn three observations into a story route.
pages.visitFit: Adult-led upper-age page for a museum-day table after a guided pause near a map, doorway, display row, or room corner.
pages.adultSetup: Have writers mark three safe observation stops in order: one start, one turn, and one finish, then keep all writing at the table.
pages.kidDirection: Map three museum observations into a story route and draft the sentence that turns the route toward its ending.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which stop changes the route and which map word helps the reader follow the paragraph.

pageSections.heading: Route Stops
lines: My first observation stop is near ____________________.
The route turns when I notice ____________________.
The finish stop should show readers ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Academy Route
lines: My story route starts with ____________________.
The middle turn changes the plan because ____________________.

pages.shareLine: Share the map word that helped your story route move: ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: The observation that became my turning point was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Stay silent and draw three route dots, then write the turning sentence: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Make a three-stop route from another room or shelf and name the turn: ____________________.

pages.title: Almost Invention Workshop Test Note
pages.notebookSkill: Transform an observed object or pattern into ordered instructions and a test note.
pages.visitFit: Adult-led notebook page for upper-age writers after noticing one object, tool shape, display pattern, or design detail.
pages.adultSetup: Ask writers to sketch or name one harmless observed design detail, then imagine a paper-only almost-invention inspired by it.
pages.kidDirection: Invent a small almost-invention from one museum clue, put three steps in order, and write a test note for the next draft.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask where a reader might get confused and which step needs a clearer order, label, or reason.

pageSections.heading: Step Order
lines: The first instruction should tell readers to ____________________.

pages.wrapUpLine: The design clue that shaped my almost-invention was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: Work quietly by revising one step and writing it here: ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Find one safe household pattern and turn it into an invented step: ____________________.

pages.title: Index Card Theater Room Cues
pages.notebookSkill: Use observed setting cues to build a short scene with a clear turn.
pages.visitFit: Adult-led upper-age notebook page for a table near a gallery, lobby, exhibit room, or quiet sketch area.
pages.adultSetup: Have writers notice three room cues such as light, shape, display order, or label placement, then arrange them like scene cards.
pages.kidDirection: Turn three museum room cues into a tiny scene, write two lines, and make the second line change the direction.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask what the first line expects, what the reply changes, and which observed cue makes the turn visible.
